summary:
Farmers in Pontianak, West Kalimantan face sudden dry spells, intense heat, and rising fuel costs for water pumps, putting crops and peatlands at high risk of failure and wildfire. We built SOLVARA to turn raw NASA satellite data into daily farm decisions.

Our platform models agrivoltaic setups by placing solar panels above crops—shading the soil to retain moisture while generating clean power for off-grid irrigation pumps. Users can view live NASA POWER solar and rainfall telemetry, inspect a 140-plot stress map, test heatwave scenarios with custom sliders, calculate monthly Rupiah fuel savings, and receive localized WhatsApp alerts.
details:
Why We Made This

Living in Pontianak, West Kalimantan, we often see local farmers struggle when sudden dry seasons and intense heat hit our area. Running fuel-powered water pumps gets very expensive, and when the peatland soil dries out too fast, crops fail and forest fires can start easily. NASA satellites actually measure sunlight, rainfall, and soil moisture every single day, but those raw numbers are hard for regular farmers to read and use on their own.

How SOLVARA Works

Our team built SOLVARA to turn NASA space data into simple tools that farmers can actually check every day. Instead of leaving crops under the hot equatorial sun, our app models agrivoltaics—which means placing solar panels right above the farm plots. The panels shade the ground so the soil stays wet longer, while also making clean electricity to run water pumps before the plants dry up.

On our dashboard, users can open the Drought & Pump Map to view live sunlight, rain, and soil wetness data straight from the NASA POWER API. You can look at global farm examples or check local Pontianak areas like Sungai Beliung, Siantan Hilir, Parit Tokaya, and Tanjung Hulu. If the soil gets too dry, the app warns about peatland fire risks and gives simple watering advice.

We also built a 140-plot field map where users can test an emergency solar pump simulation or move "What-If" sliders to see how extra hot days change water needs. Next to that, our calculator checks which parts of the Kapuas Basin fit solar panels best and shows how much money farmers can save each month in Indonesian Rupiah compared to buying fuel. Since warnings only work if people understand them, we added a phone screen preview showing WhatsApp alerts in English, Indonesian, and Arabic, along with Dark and Light screen modes.

How We Built It & Links

We coded this web app using React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS, and created our own custom SVG charts so the site loads fast without heavy libraries.

- Live Web App: https://solvara-planetary-agrivoltaics-sola-nine.vercel.app

- GitHub Code: https://github.com/azxka02-alt/SOLVARA-Planetary-Agrivoltaics-Solar-Irrigation

AI Usage Note

During this hackathon, our team used Google AI Studio to help write and organize the React code and translate the interface text into different languages. All local research about Pontianak farms, peatland fires, and project planning was done and tested by Team AFISKU.
